payload.title: How to Plan a Santorini Wedding Step by Step
payload.excerpt: Plan a Santorini wedding in nine steps: legal or symbolic, season, caldera or beach venue, guest travel, documents and questions to ask before you book.
key_takeaways: Decide first whether your Santorini ceremony will be legal or symbolic, because that choice sets your documents, your timeline and the venues that suit you.
Choose your season from the figures for Naxos, the nearest official weather station, where summer is driest and October wetter, then set the ceremony time around the heat and the north wind.
Match the setting to your guest list, because caldera terraces, hotels, wineries and private villas differ widely in capacity and guest rooms.
Put every house rule in writing before you sign, including music times, exclusive use, ceremony times and the plan if the weather turns.

faq.q: Can you legally get married in Santorini?
faq.a: Yes, but plan the legal side before the venue. As at November 2026, a marriage valid in Greece that would also have been valid under Australian law is in most cases legally recognised in Australia. For a civil marriage on the island, check the steps with the Municipality of Thira and the Australian Embassy in Athens, including any fees.

faq.q: What documents do Australians need to get married in Santorini?
faq.a: You may need to prove you are free to marry, most commonly with a Certificate of No Impediment and registry certificates, and local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, a late spouse's death certificate, and your original birth certificate and passport. Ask the Greek embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it needs an authentication or apostille.

faq.q: When is the wedding season in Santorini?
faq.a: At Naxos, the nearest official weather station, May and September have mean maximums of 22.1°C and 25.1°C against about 27°C in July and August, and October brings 38.6 mm of rain over 5.5 days. There, June to August are the driest months, while heatwaves are frequent in summer and wildfires occur from June to September. The May to October tourist season also brings crowds to the busy seaports.

faq.q: Can we have a symbolic ceremony in Santorini?
faq.a: Yes. Canaves Collection lists symbolic ceremonies alongside civil, religious and vow renewal options, and Grace Hotel offers a unity ceremony using black and white volcanic sand. You can also marry legally in Australia first and hold the symbolic ceremony on the island.

faq.q: Is Santorini good for a small wedding or elopement?
faq.a: Yes. The caldera-edge spaces in Oia and Imerovigli seat between 15 and 60, and Grace Hotel's villa terrace seats 15. Katikies lists micro weddings as a package idea, and Canaves caters for modern elopements.
